title: The Dark Side of Dataset Scaling: Evaluating Racial Classification in Multimodal Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating zero-shot image classification models using the Chicago Face Dataset (CFD) to measure the probability of assigning offensive, dehumanizing, or non-human labels (e.g., 'criminal', 'gorilla', 'chimpanzee') to images of human faces across different racial groups (Black, Latin, Asian, and White), and analyzing how these predictions change with dataset scaling.

Comparing the prediction frequencies of offensive classes (such as 'criminal') between male and female subjects from the Chicago Face Dataset to observe disparate impacts based on gender, often analyzed intersectionally with race.
